article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Indica / 40% Sativa
Genetics: Green Lantern × Double OG Chem × Long Valley Royal Kush × 98 Super Skunk
Breeder: Greenshock Farms
THC Content: 23–32%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , limonene , humulene
Primary Flavors: Skunk, diesel fuel, menthol, earth, pepper
Flowering Time (Indoor): 56–63 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Heavy
Outdoor Yield: Heavy
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

There is nothing subtle about Skunk Gas . While much of modern cannabis breeding has moved toward candy, dessert, and tropical fruit, Greenshock Farms deliberately developed this strain around the pungent qualities that once defined high-grade weed: skunk musk, diesel exhaust, damp earth, menthol, and an unmistakable funk capable of escaping a sealed container. Breeder Mark Greyshock even traces the original Skunk G-Ass name to an aroma that reminded him of a skunk exposed to gasoline—an intentionally crude description that happens to capture the plant remarkably well. The cultivar emerged from Greenshock’s long-running Northern California breeding work and later attracted broader attention through Garcia Hand Picked, whose California relaunch featured sun-grown Skunk Gas sourced from Greenshock Farms.

Beyond the provocative aroma, there is serious horticultural selection behind the name. Greenshock identified the plant during its 2023–2024 winter phenotype work, where it distinguished itself through vigor, weather resistance, yield, potency, and terpene production. Current strain documentation places total terpenes around 3–4%, with THC commonly in the mid-to-upper 20% range and exceptional tests pushing beyond 30%. This is old-school-smelling marijuana expressed through modern selection: resin-heavy, potent, productive, and rugged enough to perform indoors, in greenhouses, and under the Northern California sun.
Genetics and Lineage

Greenshock Genetics currently identifies Skunk Gas as Green Lantern × Double OG Chem × Long Valley Royal Kush × 98 Super Skunk. Each component serves a recognizable purpose in the finished cultivar. Green Lantern contributes vigor and a legacy Northern California character, while Double OG Chem pushes the pedigree toward Chem and OG-style fuel. Long Valley Royal Kush adds dense resin, earthy Kush depth, and strong outdoor breeding credentials, and 98 Super Skunk reinforces the penetrating musk that ultimately gives the hybrid its name.

Earlier breeder-authored strain reports sometimes presented a shortened pedigree—Green Lantern × Double OG Sour Chem × Long Valley Royal Kush—while current Greenshock material and commercial genetic catalogs provide the expanded lineage including 98 Super Skunk. That difference likely reflects how the underlying breeding stock was described at different stages rather than evidence of an unrelated cultivar. For a current strain reference, the expanded lineage supplied by Greenshock itself is the more appropriate version to use.

The breeding objective becomes obvious when the parents are viewed together. Nothing in this family tree was chosen to create strawberry candy or pastry terpenes. Kush, Chem, Skunk, and fuel-oriented genetics repeatedly overlap, resulting in a cultivar that preserves an increasingly uncommon style of marijuana aroma. Instead of disguising strain funk beneath sweetness, this hybrid amplifies it.
Effects and Experience

The onset can be remarkably quick. Greyshock’s original strain profile characterized the effect as moving rapidly into the head before a delayed, longer-lasting body component takes over. Early sensations may include a pronounced mental shift, elevated mood, stronger sensory awareness, and the unmistakable feeling of being very high rather than gently stimulated. For experienced consumers, that opening can feel cheerful and sociable; current cultivar descriptions use terms such as happy, smiley, stoney, and relaxing.

Physical weight becomes more important later. The initial head rush gradually gives way to a heavier body effect that can reduce the desire for activity and make relaxed evenings, music, movies, conversation, or simply doing very little more appealing. This progression helps explain why the strain is usually classified as indica dominant even though its first phase is distinctly cerebral. The transition is less like an immediate knockout and more like a strong mental high being slowly overtaken by deep physical calm.

Potency is the main reason beginners should approach it carefully. Greenshock has reported THC results as high as roughly 31%, while other documented samples fall in the mid-to-upper 20% range. At those concentrations, excessive consumption can produce anxiety, dizziness, impaired coordination, dry mouth, memory disruption, or uncomfortable sedation. The plant’s old-school aroma may suggest vintage weed, but its cannabinoid strength is thoroughly modern.
Medical Benefits

No clinical trials have evaluated Skunk Gas as a treatment for a specific medical condition, so its therapeutic reputation should not be confused with established strain-specific evidence. Historically, breeder material has associated the cultivar with pain relief and sleep, and the strong transition from cerebral effects into sustained body relaxation helps explain why some medical marijuana consumers may be interested in it for evening use. That remains experiential information rather than proof that the strain treats pain or insomnia.

Research into cannabis and cannabinoids more broadly provides a more reliable perspective. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health notes that some studies suggest modest benefits for certain forms of chronic pain, while research involving sleep has sometimes shown improved sleep quality or fewer disturbances in people with underlying health conditions. Evidence remains uncertain for many other uses, and benefits found with standardized cannabinoid preparations cannot automatically be assigned to a high-THC flower strain.

The high THC content also deserves caution in medical settings. Larger doses can cause sleepiness, dizziness, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and altered judgment, while cannabinoids may interact with medications. Anyone using marijuana for persistent pain, sleep problems, or another health condition should consider the cultivar’s potency and discuss cannabis use with an appropriate healthcare professional when medications or significant medical issues are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Skunk Gas earns its name before it ever reaches the palate. The dominant aroma is an aggressive combination of skunk spray and diesel, followed by damp earth and cooling menthol. Greenshock describes the profile as strong enough to announce itself from across a garden, an observation consistent with the breeder’s focus on terpene intensity. High Times similarly characterized the Garcia Hand Picked release as heavy in skunk, diesel, and menthol rather than the sugary profiles dominating much of the current cannabis market.

Caryophyllene, limonene, and humulene are prominent in documented material. Caryophyllene fits naturally with the cultivar’s peppery, spicy depth; humulene can support woody and earthy impressions, while limonene adds a sharper brightness that prevents the smoke from becoming completely dark and musky. Current strain records put total terpene content around 3–4%, an unusually substantial level for commercial flower.

The inhale leans toward fuel and pungent herbal spice rather than sweetness. Menthol becomes more obvious through the middle, while skunk, soil, diesel, and pepper remain on the finish. Some selections can become downright offensive in aroma—a characteristic Greenshock considers an asset. Current seed-line work descending from the original plant has produced expressions compared with dirty socks, body odor, and gym-locker funk, demonstrating just how unconventional the underlying terpene genetics can become.
Growing Information

Skunk Gas was developed under real outdoor pressure rather than selected exclusively in a tightly controlled indoor environment. Greenshock reports strong performance outdoors, indoors, and in greenhouses, with the original selection standing out for vigor and resistance to difficult winter conditions. Segra’s cultivar catalog describes a medium-height plant with moderate stretch, heavy yields, open but substantial flowers, abundant resin, and sugar leaves that can curl around dense trichome production.

Flowering generally falls around 56–63 days in current commercial cultivation references, although earlier breeder material listed approximately seven to eight weeks. Growers should therefore use trichome development and overall flower maturity rather than treating a calendar date as absolute. The buds can become sufficiently heavy to demand branch support, particularly when plants are allowed to build substantial outdoor mass. Cooler finishing temperatures may encourage lime-green flowers to darken into purple, silver, and maroon tones.

One of the plant’s most useful traits is its ability to combine substantial flower production with relatively open structure. Better spacing between flower sites improves air movement and contributes to the mold resistance Greenshock has emphasized in its outdoor selections. Even so, heavy resin and large colas warrant careful humidity management late in bloom. Proper drying is equally important: rushing the post-harvest process can strip away the volatile menthol and fuel notes that separate this weed from ordinary Kush-dominant flower.
FAQ
What strain is Skunk Gas?

Skunk Gas, originally called Skunk G-Ass, is an indica-dominant hybrid bred by Mark Greyshock of Greenshock Farms. It combines Green Lantern, Double OG Chem, Long Valley Royal Kush, and 98 Super Skunk genetics.
How strong is Skunk Gas?
Documented material generally falls around 23–32% THC. Greenshock has reported testing above 30%, making it a high-potency cultivar better suited to experienced consumers than beginners.
What does Skunk Gas smell like?

Its defining aroma combines powerful skunk with diesel fuel, earthy funk, and menthol. Peppery and herbal notes can appear underneath, while some phenotypes produce particularly unusual body-odor or locker-room-style funk.
Is Skunk Gas indica or sativa?

Breeder material has described it as approximately 60% indica and 40% sativa. Its effects support that characterization: the high begins rapidly in the head before developing into a longer-lasting and more relaxing physical experience.
How long does Skunk Gas take to flower?

Current commercial cultivation information places flowering around 56–63 days, or roughly eight to nine weeks, although older breeder material listed seven to eight weeks. Phenotype and growing environment can shift the exact finish date.
Final Thoughts on Skunk Gas

Skunk Gas represents a deliberate rejection of the idea that premium modern cannabis has to smell like candy. Greenshock Farms constructed the cultivar from proven Green Lantern, Chem, Royal Kush, and Super Skunk material, then selected for the traits that matter in a working garden: vigor, resistance, production, potency, resin, and overwhelming aroma. The resulting marijuana can exceed 3% total terpenes, push past 30% THC in exceptional batches, and still carry the skunky diesel profile associated with an earlier era of West Coast weed.

That combination is what gives the strain relevance beyond nostalgia. Its fast cerebral impact and delayed body relaxation provide substantial potency, while caryophyllene, limonene, humulene, menthol, earth, and fuel create a profile dramatically removed from today’s endless procession of fruit desserts. For consumers who actively seek pungent cannabis—and for growers who value sturdy, field-tested genetics—Skunk Gas offers something increasingly difficult to find: unapologetically offensive skunk and gas backed by serious modern breeding.
